title: Emotional Response to Different Lighting Conditions
review_question: To examine the impact of different lighting conditions (daylight, artificial, colored lights, CCT, illuminance) on human emotions, physiological and psychological reactions, memory performance, and perception, considering factors like age, cultural background, and weather.

findings.source: 12.3 How Human Eyes Adapt to Light

findings.source: 12.4 Light Sensitivity Based on Human Eyes and Age Difference

findings.source: 12.4 Light Sensitivity Based on Human Eyes and Age Difference

findings.consequent: Eye muscles, pupil size, light entry, glare, sensitivity
findings.source: 12.4 Light Sensitivity Based on Human Eyes and Age Difference
findings.quote: With older people, eye muscles tend to be weaker, causing the pupil to decrease. Therefore, less light is visible and can enter the eye, causing the eye to receive only about one-third as much light as other-aged adult persons. Due to eye muscle weakness, older people will have a harder time seeing in a dark room and their eyes are more prone to glare and sensitivity [31].

synthesis_conclusions: Humans are significantly affected by both natural and artificial lighting.
Daylight offers environmentally friendly and energy-efficient light, but glaring sunlight can make it challenging to work in some settings.
Artificial lighting impacts human physiological and psychological responses, including age-related light sensitivity, comfort levels, and the body's reactions.
There are connections between LED brightness, color temperature, melatonin suppression, and memory performance.
Artificial lighting influences mood, with effects modulated by diverse cultural contexts and weather.
Different light colors are perceived differently and influence perception, with the spectrum chart offering a wide range of colors with significant emotional impact.
Lighting design and selection are crucial for ideal human functioning.

Careful planning and choice of artificial lighting are essential to mitigate the harsh response of sunshine and the negative impacts of artificial lighting, despite daylight's energy-saving advantages.
